measurement: Measured from Luke Dean - UGC 1.mp4 (creative_assets videos/953d0ffb-6c28-4a7f-961a-4aa03b9fdc74.mp4), the 720x1280 frame at t=1.0s. White-glyph mask: luma >= 175 inside the caption band. Mask bounds x 198-512, y 385-525. Cap height 27px (line 1, y 385-411). TikTok Sans wght 500 at opsz 36 has a 26px cap at em 37, so the size is 37/720 of the frame width. Line tops sit at 385, 424, 462 and 500, a pitch of 39px = 1.054em. The block centre is the mask midpoint, 455/1280 of the source height. The stroke is an outside edge, 2px at 720 wide (0.054054 of the em). On the Luke stem against the black ceiling the fringe is the two near-black pixels beside the white core; where the letters meet the hand it is the two dark pixels (luma 33 then 1) before the skin. Glyph check: height-normalised per-glyph IoU of line 2 against TikTok Sans 500 averaged 0.74; the diagnostic f and g matched it better than Circular Std, Helvetica or Arial Bold. SF Pro scored 0.75 overall and is not separable from TikTok Sans once the 720p stroke is included, so the brief's font stands. The variable font's wdth axis defaults to 100, which draws these lines about 14% narrower than the frame; wdth 120 matches the ink widths (line 2 about 315px). CSS font-weight does not move the wght axis, so the composition sets font-variation-settings. The stroke sits behind the fill. The weight is the wght axis, chosen by stem width at 720 wide with that 2px stroke and wdth 120. Half-max white core of the l in Luke: reference 3.78px, wght 500 4.94px, wght 450 4.19px, wght 400 3.95px. The i in joins is 3.80px on the reference; the i in the word in is 4.90px, 4.20px and 3.97px at those weights. 400 matches. An l at weight 400 and wdth 100, 120 and 140 measures 3.86px, 3.97px and 4.03px, so the width axis stays 120. Method and the comparison box: reference/reference.json.
